title: Federation
parity_no_reports_hint: Reports are generated when there are transactions with federated nodes.
parity_fc_remote_hint: The remote node has not shared its CF
limits_propose_desc: Select a federated node and propose new limits. The other node must confirm.
limits_no_federated_hint: To propose a bilateral limit, you must first register a peer node.
limits_no_bilateral: No custom bilateral limits. All nodes use the base limit.
limits_change_hint: This request will go to the assembly for voting. Members will decides whether to approve the change.
merge_how_works_desc: When two nodes federate, if there are users registered in both with the same national ID, both assemblies must agree on which node each person stays and what to do with the balance. While there are unresolved conflicts, federation cannot be completed.
merge_scan_desc: Enter the domain of the other node to search for duplicate users by national ID.
merge_no_conflicts_hint: Scan another node to detect duplicates.
merge_blocked_hint: Blocked - both assemblies must reach consensus
merge_which_node: Which node does the user stay in?
merge_no_dual: Dual membership is not allowed. The user stays in one node only.
merge_balance_action: What to do with the balances?
merge_forgive_debt: Forgive debt of the removed node
merge_remove_balance: Discard balance of the removed node
discover_federation_personal: Federation is done personally, not automatically
discover_federation_personal_desc: This system does NOT federate nodes with one click. The public key for federating is shared personally between people, not through the system. Here you only see information about other nodes (country, location, governance, web, contact) so you can communicate with them directly. The idea is to have human contact, for people to meet, for assemblies to approve, and then share keys in person.
discover_how_works_desc: There is no central server. Each node shares its list of known nodes with federated nodes, and they in turn share it with theirs. Thus, it is enough for one node to federate with just one other for the entire network to discover it. To federate, contact the person responsible for the other node personally and exchange public keys.
discover_search_placeholder: Search by domain, name, country or location...
discover_federated_hint: Federated nodes are not removed even if they are offline. They only show their current status.
discover_no_discovered_hint: Federate with a node to start discovering more nodes in the network via gossip.
discover_inactive_desc: These nodes were marked as inactive because all nodes in the network reported that they cannot connect with them. It is not that a single node could not (it may not have internet), but that all confirmed it does not respond. They are kept internally to continue checking if they reappear someday, but are not shown in the main list.
discover_requests_not_auto: Contact requests do not federate automatically. They are a way to express interest and share contact information.
discover_auto_federation: Global automatic federation: When confirming a pairing with 4-option verification, the new node enters the entire federated network automatically. The sponsor propagates the new node's info to all its peers in exponential chain, and each node establishes an individual 1-to-1 relationship. You do not need to manually federate with each node.
discover_fed_pairings_desc: A new node requests to federate. The new node communicated a 6-digit code by phone. Click Confirm to see 4 options and choose the correct one. Upon confirming, the node will enter the entire federated network automatically via chain propagation.
discover_select_code: Choose the code communicated by the new node:
discover_federate_hint: To federate: contact this person personally, review your governance, assemblies approve, and then share public keys in person. It is not federated with one click.
discover_no_sent_requests: You have not sent any requests
discover_config_desc: Configure how often your node shares its list, verifies if nodes are active, and cleans up inactive ones. Each node can have its own configuration.
discover_share_interval_hint: How often your node shares its list of known nodes with peers. Default: 24 hours.
discover_health_interval_hint: How often your node verifies if discovered nodes are still active. Default: 168 hours (7 days). An inactive node is decided by consensus of the entire network, not by your single check.
discover_cleanup_interval_hint: How often inactive nodes are removed from the visible list. They are kept internally to continue checking. Default: 365 days.
discover_max_failed_hint: How many times a node must fail your verification before requesting consensus from other nodes. Default: 3.
discover_request_modal_desc: You will send a contact request to another node. This does not federate automatically. The other node will see your information and can contact you personally to federate.
discover_request_contact_hint: How the other node can contact you
gov_no_proposals_hint: Create a proposal to change a value that affects the entire federation.
gov_auto_applied: Change applied automatically on all nodes.
gov_constants_federated: These constants are federated: they are the same on all nodes. They cannot be edited directly. To change them, create a proposal in the New Proposal tab.
gov_new_proposal_desc: Propose a change that will affect all nodes in the federation. All federated nodes will have to approve the change. When consensus is reached, the change is applied automatically.
gov_which_constant: Which constant do you want to change?
gov_no_known_nodes: No known nodes. This is the only node.
gov_expelled_desc: These nodes were expelled by federation vote. To re-enter, they must request admission again and will automatically accept all existing rules.
gov_expel_domain: Domain of the node to expel
gov_expel_reason_hint: Explain why this node should be expelled. All nodes will see this reason when voting.
gov_vote_consensus: Vote registered. Consensus reached - change applied automatically.
gov_must_enter_value: You must enter a proposed value
gov_must_enter_domain: You must enter the domain of the node to expel
peers_your_pub_key: Your public key (share with other nodes):
peers_no_peers_hint: To federate with another node, register its domain and public key here, and ask the other node to register your public key.
peers_sponsorships_desc: Active sponsorships show the nodes that your node is backing as a sponsor. The limit held by each sponsorship is released when the sponsored node reaches Level 2.
peers_block_confirm: Block trade with {{domain}}? This will stop all transactions with that node. Only affects your node.
peers_block_success: Trade blocked with {{domain}}. Propagated to all peers.
peers_remove_confirm: Remove {{domain}} from the discovered nodes list?
gov_federated_gov_desc: Some values affect the ENTIRE federation (like the internal basic basket). They cannot be changed per individual node. To change them, a proposal is created and all federated nodes must approve it.
gov_default_threshold: By default 75% of nodes are required
gov_default_threshold_desc: (majority must approve). This threshold can be changed, but changing it requires approval under the current threshold. That is: if the current threshold is 75%, changing it to 100% or 50%+1 requires approval under 75%. Once changed, future proposals are approved with the new threshold.
gov_single_node_auto: When there is only one node, its proposals are auto-approved (it is 100% of 1 node). New nodes joining the federation accept existing policies.
gov_expel_warning_desc: This is a serious action. An expulsion proposal is created that nodes must approve (under the current threshold, default 75%). If approved, the expelled node cannot participate in the federation. To re-enter, it must request admission again and will automatically accept all existing rules.
limits_credit_hint: Maximum positive balance (in your favor) with this node.
limits_debit_hint: Maximum negative balance (debt) with this node.
discover_remove_confirm: Remove {{domain}} from the discovered nodes list?
discover_fed_confirmed: Node federated and confirmed successfully. Propagating to the entire network automatically...
gov_nodes_desc: Here appear all nodes that belong to the federation, even if you are not federated directly with all. Global decisions (votes) apply to all nodes on the network, because they form a chain: if A is federated with B, and B with C, decisions from A affect C even if they are not directly federated.
parity_help_what: Parity measures whether the exchange between your node and another federated node is balanced or unbalanced. It is like a scale: on one side are the things you receive from the other node (imports) and on the other side what you send (exports).
parity_help_ratio: It is the result of dividing imports by exports.
parity_help_balanced: Balanced: you import and export the same.
parity_help_import_more: You import more than you export (e.g: 1.5 = you import 50% more).
parity_help_export_more: You export more than you import (e.g: 0.5 = you export double).
parity_help_only_import_desc: You have received products but never sent anything.
parity_help_only_export_desc: You have sent products but never received anything.
parity_help_imports: Total TQ received from the other node (purchases).
parity_help_exports: Total TQ sent to the other node (sales).
parity_help_balance: Exports minus imports. Positive = you are owed. Negative = you owe.
parity_help_fc_no_affect: The FC does NOT affect the price of products. If you go to another node with your card and buy a product that costs 50, they charge you 50. The price is the same as what is published in the store. There is no conversion or price change between nodes.
parity_help_fc_exterior: The FC is used exclusively in external trade: when External Trade buys products internally to sell abroad or when it buys products from abroad to bring them to the node.
parity_help_fc_reference: The FC also serves as an informational reference so members know how much a product is worth in local currency if they decide to pay directly between themselves.
parity_help_fc_local: Your Conversion Factor. It is how much 1 unit of currency is worth in energy (kWh).
parity_help_fc_remote: The Conversion Factor of the other node. Only appears if the other node has shared it.
parity_help_purpose_label: What is the parity report for?
parity_help_purpose_1: Detect unbalanced trade relationships between nodes.
parity_help_purpose_2: Decide whether to adjust bilateral limits with a node.
parity_help_purpose_3: Promote exports where there is a deficit.
parity_help_purpose_4: Encourage exchanges in areas where there is a surplus.
parity_help_imbalance_label: What to do if there is an imbalance?
parity_help_imbalance_1: If you import a lot: look for local products you can export to the other node.
parity_help_imbalance_2: If you export a lot: consider importing products you need from the other node.
parity_help_imbalance_3: If it is balanced: maintain the current trade relationship.
parity_help_suggestions: The system shows suggestions when it detects imbalances. If parity is high, it suggests increasing the bilateral limit. If there is disparity, it suggests not increasing the limit.
gov_process_1: You create the proposal (your node auto-approves)
gov_process_2: The proposal is shared with all federated nodes
gov_process_4: When the current threshold is reached (default 75% = majority), the change applies to all
gov_process_5: If consensus is not reached, the current value continues to be used
gov_threshold_change_desc: To change the approval threshold, a proposal is created like any other. That proposal is approved under the current threshold. Once approved, future proposals use the new threshold.
gov_expel_important_1: The proposal is created with the current threshold (default 75%)
gov_expel_important_2: All nodes must approve for it to apply
gov_expel_important_3: If approved, the node will not be able to federate or trade
gov_expel_important_4: The expelled node can request re-entry later
gov_expel_important_5: Upon re-entry, it automatically inherits all existing rules
peers_help_what: Federation is a mechanism that connects your local node with nodes from other communities, allowing users on your exchange network to trade with users from other federated networks, without needing a bank or central entity.
peers_help_purpose: It allows extending the reach of your exchange network beyond your local community.
peers_help_peer: A peer node is another exchange network node that has registered in your system to establish a federated connection.
peers_help_register: Click Register Node Peer, complete the form with the domain, name and public key of the other node, and save.
peers_help_domain: It is the unique identifier of the node on the federated network, normally an internet domain name.
peers_help_keys: They are cryptographic identifiers based on the Ed25519 algorithm (64 hexadecimal characters) that uniquely identify each node.
peers_help_comm: When two nodes federate with each other, they establish a secure channel using their public keys. Transactions between users of different nodes are sent via HTTPS, cryptographically signed.
peers_help_state_active: The node is registered and federation is mutual (both have registered each other).
peers_help_state_pending: The node is registered on your side but the other node has not registered you yet.
peers_help_state_mutual: Indicates that both nodes have registered each other and federation is active.
peers_help_levels_desc: Each node has a level that determines its limit and capabilities:
peers_help_level1: Limit 1,000 TQ, no vote, no sponsorship. Minimum 90 days before promotion.
peers_help_level2: Limit 5,000 TQ, with vote and sponsorship capability. Achieved by federation vote.
peers_help_level3: Limit 20,000 TQ. Automatic promotion upon meeting reciprocity and average limit.
peers_help_effective: A node's effective limit is its nominal limit minus the limit retained by active sponsorships.
peers_help_pool: In addition to bilateral balances between node pairs, there is a shared global pool. The balance you earn on one node is spendable on any other federated node.
peers_help_usage: Copy your public key and send it to the admin of the other node. Ask for the other node's public key. Register the other node here. Ask the other node to register you.
peers_help_auto: When a new node federates with a sponsor via 4-option verification, the sponsor automatically propagates the new node's info to all its peers in an exponential chain.
peers_help_block: You can block trade with a specific node without needing an agreement. It only affects your node.
limits_help_what: They are the maximum balance limits (positive or negative) your node can have with each federated peer node. They serve to control risk.
limits_help_purpose: They allow managing credit risk between federated nodes. Without limits, a node could accumulate unlimited debt with another.
limits_help_credit: It is the maximum positive balance your node can have with another node. That is, the maximum the other node can owe you.
limits_help_debit: It is the maximum negative balance (debt) your node can have with another node. That is, the maximum your node can owe the other.
limits_help_trade: When a user on your node buys something from a user on another federated node, the bilateral balance changes. The system verifies that limits are not exceeded before approving the transaction.
limits_help_global: Maximum total debt/balance of the node with the entire federated network. Applies to all nodes at the base level.
limits_help_bilateral: Customized limit between two specific nodes. If two nodes agree on a higher limit, it does NOT consume the global limit.
limits_help_effective: The effective limit between two nodes = min(limit_A_to_B, limit_B_to_A). Both nodes must raise it for the new value to apply.
limits_help_base: Initial limit equal for all pairs (e.g: 50% of global). Can be customized later node by node.
limits_help_thresholds: Percentages of the limit (e.g: 50%/75%/90%) that trigger notifications when the balance approaches the limit.
limits_help_usage: Review the global configuration. To customize the limit with a specific node, click Propose Bilateral, select the node and enter the new limits.
merge_error_enter_domain: Enter the domain of the other node
merge_conflicts_detected: {{count}} conflicts detected. Review and propose resolutions.
merge_no_conflicts_clean: There are no conflicts. Nodes can federate without duplicates.
merge_confirm_execute: Confirm execution of the resolution? This action will migrate the user and process the balance.
merge_combine_desc: Combine: sum both balances (positive+positive=more positive, negative+negative=more negative, positive+negative=they cancel out).
federation_sync_desc2: between federated nodes. When a node changes its domain, IP, WireGuard or services, all others receive it automatically. You don't need to share anything manually.
federation_sync_started: Sync started. Federated nodes will receive the updated info.
federation_no_peers: There are no federated nodes with network info.
federation_no_peers_hint: Federate with another community in "Federate Communities" to view its info here.
peers_method_auto_desc: Use the 4-option verification on the Node Discovery page. Upon confirmation, the node will automatically federate with the entire network via chain propagation.
peers_manual_step1: Copy your public key (above) and send it to the admin of the other node
peers_manual_step2: Ask for the other node's public key
peers_manual_step3: Register the other node here (domain + public key)
peers_manual_step4: Ask the other node to register you
peers_manual_step5: When both have registered each other, federation is active
peers_manual_note: Note: The manual method only registers the peer locally. For the new node to join the entire network automatically, use the 4-option verification.
